reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every natural number n with n ≥ 3 and every real κ with κ ≥ 4, let j₀ = 0 in Fin n, let O(n) be the full real orthogonal matrix group (including both determinant signs), and let μ be its normalized Haar probability measure, namely Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : PositiveCompacts O(n)). For O ∈ O(n), set
A(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) Iₙ − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ).
Define the explicit real functions
p(O,v) = sqrt(det A(O)) / (2π)^(n/2) · exp(−vᵀ A(O) v / 2), for real coordinate vectors v : Fin n → ℝ,
and
r(O,x) = sqrt(det A(O)) / (2π)^(n/2) · exp(−(κ + 1 − (κ − 1)O₀₀) ‖x‖₂² / 4), for x ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
Here sqrt is the nonnegative real square root; (2π)^(n/2) uses the real exponent (n : ℝ)/2. The matrix products and quadratic form use the coordinates, and ‖x‖₂ is the actual Euclidean norm, not the coordinate supremum norm. Write vₓ = WithLp.ofLp x for the underlying coordinate vector of x.
Then for every x ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), both functions O ↦ det(O) p(O,vₓ) and O ↦ det(O) r(O,x) are absolutely Bochner L¹ integrable with respect to μ, and
∫_{O(n)} det(O) p(O,vₓ) dμ(O) = ∫_{O(n)} det(O) r(O,x) dμ(O).
The two L¹ assertions and the integral equality are simultaneous conclusions for each fixed x. The functions p and r are the literal displayed formulas; no probability-law construction or density characterization is assumed.

All displayed functions and integrals are real-valued. Integration variable O has normalized full-group Haar probability μ. The norm is Euclidean, and WithLp.ofLp x supplies coordinates without changing the norm.
semantic_slots.quantifiers: For every n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 3, for every κ ∈ ℝ with κ ≥ 4, after defining j₀, p and r, for every Euclidean vector x, the two integrability statements and the equality hold. In each of these three conclusions, O is bound by integration or the corresponding integrability function.
semantic_slots.assumptions: The only parameter restrictions are n ≥ 3 and κ ≥ 4. The first-index validity follows from n ≥ 3. The actual normalized Haar law, topology, Borel structure and Euclidean norm are the approved ambient definitions. There is no integrability assumption and no density-characterization assumption.
semantic_slots.conclusion: For each fixed x, O ↦ det(O)p(O,WithLp.ofLp x) and O ↦ det(O)r(O,x) are both absolutely Bochner L¹ integrable under μ, and their real integrals under μ are equal. Each integrand retains the signed factor det(O).

All integration is over the full orthogonal group rather than a determinant component. The claim compares these two signed integrals, with both L¹ assertions, for every x.

A(O) and the prefactor depend on n, κ and O. p additionally depends on v; r additionally depends on x through its squared Euclidean norm, while its exponent uses O₀₀. No unspecified constants, existence choices or source-dependent objects appear; 2, 4 and π are literal constants.
